title: Supply curve runway grid and staffing phase sim
content:
Purpose
This is a working simulation (sheet-style) to connect per-unit inference economics to a 12-week runway projection and a 6-month phased hiring plan. Goal: surface which hires or price moves buy the most runway under realistic capacity and latency constraints. NOT final — iterative model for FY27 planning run.

High-level framing / what to use it for
- Quick answers to: if average price per 1k tokens moves +/- 10%, how many FTEs can we afford and what is the runway delta?
- Map GPU capacity (reserved vs burst) into monthly cash out and effective per-token cost by latency tier.
- Provide hiring triggers for retention of key infra/ops skills vs delaying customer success hires.

Assumptions (editable in Assumptions tab)
- Avg token consumption per active customer per month: 1.2M tokens
- Forecasted active customers (M0..M5): 200, 260, 320, 380, 450, 520
- Price per 1k tokens (hosted API blended): Base $0.06, Conservative $0.05, Premium $0.07
- GPU reserved cost (amortized per month): $210k (covers 60% baseline throughput)
- Burst GPU cost (spot/short-term): $70k per 10% of incremental throughput on top of reserved
- Avg infra engineering fully-loaded cost / month per FTE: $18k
- Avg product/pm fully-loaded cost / month per FTE: $16.5k
- Avg SRE fully-loaded cost / month per FTE: $19k
- Avg CS fully-loaded cost / month per FTE: $12k
- Other fixed monthly opex: $95k

Scenario Grid (summary table)
Columns: Scenario | Price/1k | Effective cost/1k | Gross margin | Monthly revenue | Monthly token volume | GPU spend | HC spend | Other opex | Net burn change | Runway delta (vs Base months)
Rows:
Base | $0.060 | $0.0125 | 79% | $720,000 | 12,000,000 | $210,000 | $420,000 | $95,000 | -$5,000 | 0
Accelerate (higher price + adoption) | $0.070 | $0.0130 | 81% | $1,040,000 | 14,857,143 | $260,000 | $560,000 | $95,000 | +$120,000 | +1.8 months
Conserve (lower price, slower growth) | $0.050 | $0.0115 | 77% | $600,000 | 12,000,000 | $210,000 | $360,000 | $95,000 | -$70,000 | -1.1 months
High-Volume Discount (aggressive commit slab) | $0.045 | $0.0098 | 78% | $1,350,000 | 30,000,000 | $500,000 | $900,000 | $95,000 | -$145,000 | -2.5 months

Notes on table construction:
- Effective cost/1k includes GPU amortization + bandwidth + storage slices borne by inference (calculated from GPU reserved + burst divided by token volumes).
- HC spend is the staffed plan cost for that month (see Staffing Plan tab).
- Net burn change is revenue minus all cash outflows; positive means runway extension.

Staffing Plan (6-month phased hires) - snapshot of hires and phasing assumptions
Columns: Month | Eng infra | SRE | Product | CS | Total new hires | Cumulative HC | HC cost/month
M0 (now) | 28 | 6 | 5 | 8 | 0 | 47 | $874,000
M1 | 30 | 7 | 5 | 9 | +3 (2 eng infra, 1 CS) | 50 | $934,000
M2 | 32 | 8 | 6 | 10 | +4 (2 eng infra, 1 SRE, 1 PM) | 54 | $1,010,000
M3 | 34 | 9 | 7 | 12 | +5 (2 eng infra, 1 SRE, 2 CS) | 59 | $1,123,000
M4 | 36 | 10 | 8 | 14 | +4 (1 eng infra, 1 PM, 2 CS) | 63 | $1,192,000
M5 | 37 | 10 | 9 | 15 | +3 (1 eng infra, 1 PM, 1 SRE) | 66 | $1,255,000

Hiring phasing rationale bullets:
- Early hires prioritized for infra engineering to reduce cost/1k via batching/quantization projects (two hires per cycle until hit 36 infra engs).
- SRE hires spaced to support canary/dedicated pools and reduce burst spend; first SRE hires bring tooling to reduce spot spend by 8-12%.
- CS hires backloaded slightly to preserve runway; ramp when MRR > $800k and churn signals below 2.2%.
- Product hires tied to rollout of Optimize features (pricing experiment tooling) — timed at M2 and M4.

Runway simulation excerpt (12 weeks)
- Start cash cushion: $18.5M
- Weekly base burn without hires: $420k
- Incremental weekly burn per scheduled hires: week 1-4: +$40k/wk, week 5-8 +$55k/wk, week 9-12 +$30k/wk (reflects hiring cadence and ramp of full benefits)
- Scenario toggles: price +/- 10%, burst GPU spend +/- 25%, adoption +/- 20%
Example quick outputs (approx):
- Base price, base adoption: runway ~44 weeks
- Price -10% & burst +25% & hiring plan executed: runway ~37 weeks (-7 weeks)
- Price +10% & adoption +20% & hiring paused for 6 weeks: runway ~52 weeks (+8 weeks)

Key decision triggers (Triggers tab)
- If monthly revenue > $1.0M for two consecutive months -> greenlight CS hires at planned cadence and open 2 more customer success seats.
- If burst spend > 22% of GPU budget for 4 consecutive weeks -> hire 1 SRE and prioritize spot-cost reduction automations.
- If churn > 2.5% -> pause 1 round of CS hires and reallocate budget to targeted retention programs.
- If average 95th latency tier increases 20% while burst spend remains > 15% -> prioritize infra hires to refactor KV caching path.

Open questions / TODOs
- Validate effective cost/1k with infra team (Marco) — current model uses a rough amortization; need a per-region split.
- Confirm recruiting pipeline dates for infra (Aisha to share earliest start dates) and update ramp assumptions.
- Run sensitivity sweep for 18-month horizon (currently 12-week/6-month focused).

How to use this doc in practice
- Edit Assumptions tab first (all green cells) to reflect latest region mix and reserved capacity commitments.
- Toggle Scenario Grid drop-down to run quick comparisons.
- Use Triggers tab to convert simulation outputs into hiring checklist items for hiring manager review.

Comments: this sheet intentionally biases early infra investment to reduce per-token cost because small delta in cost/1k compounds across high-volume customers. But the team should sanity-check the timing risk vs revenue growth cadence.

Recent changes log:
- 2026-11-18 Lina Chen: initial draft and base scenario table created.
- 2026-11-25 Marco Ruiz: updated burst cost assumptions based on regional spot runbook.
- 2026-12-03 Aisha Patel: adjusted HC costs and added hiring trigger for churn.

Bottom line / ask to finance leaders:
- Review and push back on the assumed GPU amortization and approved headcount ramp in M2-M4.
- If acceptable, convert to a formal sheet and surface to execs with one-pager summarizing runway deltas for board package.
